brief: A month ago, the author flagged Taiwan's crowded AI positioning, accelerating foreign outflows, and stretched divergence versus Korea and semiconductors, judging fundamentals strong but expectations extreme and the market vulnerable to a catch-down. That catch-down has now happened: EWT has fallen 34% from its all-time high, sits below its 200-day moving average, and has closed its gap with EWY. An EWT December 95 put flagged less than a month ago as a cheap catch-down trade has risen from $2 to almost $20, nearly 10x. Foreign investors sold another $6bn last week, taking YTD net selling to $99bn (Goldman), $75bn from TSMC alone. Hedge funds have cut Taiwan exposure further this month via long liquidation and fresh shorts: net allocation fell to the 24th percentile over the past year (85th over five years), gross allocation to the 89th percentile over five years. Taiwan is now the biggest underweight for both Asian (530bps) and global EM (425bps) active funds, and its usual Q4-into-Chinese New Year seasonal strength is not showing up. Weekly RSI has collapsed at a pace not seen since the Covid crash. The desk is not yet buying the dip but says the extremes are hard to ignore.
